title: Empirical Integration of a Formal Network Verifier as an Oracle inside an LLM Generate–Verify–Repair Loop: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired within-task experiment to test whether embedding a formal-network verifier as an oracle inside a bounded LLM Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) loop increases detection/rejection of unsafe or incorrect LLM-generated network configurations and improves bounded repair success versus single-shot generation. We ran N=270 intent→configuration tasks (3 vendor-style syntaxes × 3 topology templates × 30 tasks) in a paired design using gpt-5-mini. A deterministic netops validator/emulator provided ground truth. All 540 planned episodes completed. Both baseline (single-shot generation) and guarded (generate → verifier → bounded repair if rejected) arms accepted 270/270 configurations (100%), giving a paired difference of 0.00 (95% CI 0.00–0.00; exact McNemar two-sided p=1.0). The preregistered primary estimand therefore shows no improvement from the inserted verifier under these tasks and model settings. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, model-call traces, scoring traces, and analysis artifacts to enable reproducibility and interpret the null result with respect to dataset difficulty, generator behavior, verifier design, and the chosen shared-initial generation semantics.

sections.introduction: LLM-driven intent→configuration pipelines promise simpler NetOps but raise safety and correctness concerns: stochastic generation can produce incorrect or unsafe device commands. A pragmatic mitigation pattern is Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR), where a deterministic verifier rejects unsafe candidates and provides diagnostics for bounded automated repair. We asked (preregistered): does embedding a formal-network verifier as an oracle inside a bounded GVR loop increase detection/rejection of unsafe or incorrect LLM-generated configurations and improve bounded repair success versus single-shot generation? We contribute (1) a preregistered paired experiment (study_id netverify_gvr_empirical_integration_2026_v1) with full provenance and artifact hashes; (2) a synthetic intent→configuration task suite and Dockerized emulator/validator used as deterministic ground truth; (3) complete execution and analysis artifacts showing the observed outcome; (4) an evidence-grounded discussion of why the inserted verifier produced no detectable change and what this implies for operational evaluation.
sections.related_work: This work builds on prior generate–verify–repair proposals and verifier-in-the-loop architectures for safety-critical code/configuration generation (e.g., Cadenas' convergent-correctness GVR framing [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899]) and formal verification applied to networks (e.g., NetKAT/NetKAT-derived verification techniques and quantitative NetKAT analyses [doi:10.1145/3808318]). Prior intent-based NetOps and RAG/agentic-NetOps surveys motivated task selection and validator semantics. Unlike broad benchmark papers that compare many LLMs on static question sets, our experiment evaluates an operational question about a verifier oracle's marginal effect under a preregistered, reproducible paired design.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: The full preregistration JSON (study_id netverify_gvr_empirical_integration_2026_v1) was frozen before observing outcomes (see preregistration SHA-256 8ae7fbadf89e5d56671560e43f03c4a92ad5f8c9b8586ac8eb3cc3c8fa00a1c0 recorded in the evidence bundle). Design: paired within-task; N=270 distinct intent→configuration tasks (3 vendor syntaxes × 3 topology templates × 30 tasks). For each task we executed two conditions on the same generated candidate: baseline = single-shot generation scored by the deterministic verifier; guarded = identical generation candidate routed through the verifier and, if rejected, a single bounded LLM repair call (maximum repair calls per task = 1). Important preregistered generation_semantics: shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false) — both arms evaluated the same initial generation for each task. This choice is recorded in the preregistration and the execution manifest (see execution/execution_manifest.json; model configuration recorded in execution/model_configuration.json, sha256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Model and prompting: gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses) with deterministic prompt templates and fixed seeds; model_calls_used=270 because the shared-initial semantics produced one initial generation per pair (manifest and per-call trace files are archived). Validator and emulator: a deterministic netops validator/emulator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) running in Dockerized Kathará/Mininet environment provided executable ground truth for intent constraints and device-state simulation. Validation subset: a preregistered 20% stratified sample (54 tasks) was reserved for verifier vs emulator concordance checks (see execution/scoring/ and analysis/ artifacts). Analysis plan: primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline assessed with an exact McNemar two-sided test; paired-bootstrap percentile CIs (10k resamples, seed=1729) reported per preregistration; subgroup analyses (3×3) Bonferroni-corrected.
sections.results: Execution and primary outcome: All 540 planned episodes completed without infrastructure exclusions (execution/execution_manifest.json; artifact hashes included in the evidence bundle). Because of the shared-initial generation semantics, the experiment used one initial generation per pair (model_calls_used=270 recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json). Observed outcomes: baseline accepted = 270/270 (100%), guarded accepted = 270/270 (100%); contingency: n11=270, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Verifier–emulator concordance: on the preregistered validation subset (54 reserved tasks) the verifier verdicts matched emulator ground truth for all checked cases: verifier false-accept = 0, verifier false-reject = 0, concordance 54/54 = 100%. (Per-task scorer traces and JSONs recorded under execution/scoring/; representative scoring files include execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha350bfaa2e..., execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json sha be7cf7c1..., and execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json sha c06246bf...; full lists and hashes appear in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts.) Representative examples: task-000001 (intent and normalized accepted configuration) and its scoring JSON are at execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha350bfaa2eec0...); the generator produced the same candidate for baseline and guarded arms (see execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt sha f8de4d6e...). Artifacts: paired contingency table and condition summary are in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha62cd99d7...) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha9f43d7b4...), respectively. All raw model responses, provider traces, scoring outputs, and per-episode validator traces are archived (execution/*) with SHA-256 hashes in the execution manifest for reproducibility.
sections.discussion: Why a null (zero) paired difference? Under the preregistered shared-initial-generation semantics, the generator (gpt-5-mini with the fixed prompt/templates) produced verifier-acceptable candidates for every task in the synthetic suite; therefore the verifier never rejected any initial candidate and the bounded repair path was not invoked. This outcome is an empirical fact supported by the per-episode scoring artifacts and the analysis contingency table. Interpretation: (1) When model generations are already compliant with the verifier rules (the observed regime), inserting the verifier oracle and a bounded repair budget produces no measurable gain in detection/rejection; (2) this does not imply a verifier is unnecessary operationally—verifiers provide traceability and can detect failures in harsher conditions; (3) the result highlights the dependence of observed verifier utility on task difficulty, prompt/schema design, generator sampling behavior, verifier conservatism, and repair budget. Operational implications: future evaluations should (a) test independent-condition generation (per-condition fresh samples) instead of shared-initial candidates to assess end-to-end detection under generator variability, (b) include adversarial or out-of-distribution intents, (c) vary model temperature and sampling to explore stochastic failure modes, (d) test multiple verifier rule-sets (conservative vs permissive) and larger repair budgets, and (e) extend to multiple LLM families and vendor-exact CLI idiosyncrasies.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, reproducible paired experiment to test whether a formal-network verifier as an oracle inside a bounded GVR loop increases detection/rejection or repair success. Under the chosen synthetic tasks, fixed prompts, and model (gpt-5-mini) with shared-initial-generation semantics, the verifier did not change outcomes: both arms produced verifier-acceptable configurations for all N=270 tasks (paired difference 0.00, 95% CI 0.00–0.00, exact McNemar p=1.0). The complete artifact set—including the preregistration, model-call traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces, paired contingency table, and hashes—is released to enable follow-up experiments that vary task hardness, generation semantics, model sampling, verifier conservatism, and repair budgets. Null results like this one are informative when experiments are preregistered and fully reproducible: they delineate where an intervention does or does not change outcomes and guide stronger operational evaluations.

limitations: Synthetic task suite and limited operational realism: results may not generalize to complex, noisy, adversarial, or production NetOps environments.
Single-model evaluation: only gpt-5-mini was tested; results do not imply multi-model generality.

Shared-initial-generation semantics: both arms evaluated the same initial generated candidate (independent_condition_generation=false). This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used=270 (one initial generation per pair) and constrains interpretation: the experiment measures the verifier's marginal effect on the same candidates rather than on independently sampled per-condition generations.
Bounded repair budget: the repair loop allowed at most one repair call per rejected candidate; multi-step or larger budgets were not evaluated and could change outcomes.

Verifier rule-set sensitivity: we tested a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); different verifier conservatism or rule-sets may change false-accept/reject trade-offs and observed utility.
Emulator vs production gap: emulator-validated safety does not guarantee identical behavior on heterogeneous vendor devices or live production networks.
